classification.difficultyReason: Infer that each base dimension loses twice the cut-out side length, model their product as the given area and reject a root that makes the box dimensions impossible.

content.prompt:
A metal sheet is 50 cm wide and 60 cm long. It has squares cut out of the corners so that it can be folded to form a box with a base area of $1200\text{ cm}^2$. Find the length of the side of the squares.

Introduce a pronumeral, write down a quadratic equation and solve it.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the side length of each square. The base measures $(50-2x)$ cm by $(60-2x)$ cm, with $0<x<25$.
$$\begin{align*}(50-2x)(60-2x)&=1200\\3000-220x+4x^2&=1200\\4x^2-220x+1800&=0\\x^2-55x+450&=0\\(x-10)(x-45)&=0\\x&=10\text{ or }45\end{align*}$$
Reject $45$ because the base dimensions would be negative. Each square has side length $10\text{ cm}$. Check: $(50-20)(60-20)=1200\text{ cm}^2$.
